h1: The 5 Best Docking Stations for 4K 120Hz Monitors of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five docks for 4K 120Hz monitors, covering DisplayLink, KVM and Thunderbolt options and which ones really state 120Hz.
summary: The TobenONE 18-in-1 DL7400 is our best overall for Windows users, with quad 4K at 120Hz. The 4K120Hz KVM dock is the pick if you share monitors between two computers, and the USB C dual-monitor dock is the budget route to 4K at up to 144Hz. The Plugable Thunderbolt 4 dock is the driverless option for new MacBooks.
intro: Plenty of docks say 4K on the box and quietly cap you at 60Hz once two monitors are plugged in. A 4K 120Hz monitor needs a dock that states that refresh rate for your exact setup, and the stated figure is the first thing to check, not the port count.

We reviewed five docks on paper, ranking them on stated refresh rate, number of displays, host compatibility and extras like charging and Ethernet. Three of the five state high refresh rates directly. The other two are included as alternates, and you should verify refresh on those listings.

products.name: TobenONE 18-in-1 DisplayLink Docking Station (DL7400)
products.verdict: Quad 4K at 120Hz and five HDMI outputs, for Windows.
products.description:
The TobenONE DL7400 is an 18-in-1 DisplayLink dock that supports up to five monitors, with quad 4K at 120Hz on Windows. It has five HDMI outputs with a cooling fan, 45W fast charging and 2.5GbE Ethernet.

It ranks first because it states 4K at 120Hz across several screens, which none of the others do. Compared with the KVM dock below it, you get more displays, though you must install a driver and it is Windows-focused.

Buy it for multi-monitor Windows desks. The caveat is the driver install and the $200-500 price tier.
products.idealFor: Windows users running several monitors at 4K 120Hz.
products.skipIf: You use a Mac or dislike drivers.

products.name: KVM Switch 2 Monitors 2 Computers Docking Station, 4K60Hz/4K120Hz
products.verdict: Switch two monitors between two PCs with a stated 4K120Hz path.
products.description:
This 13-in-1 KVM dock drives two monitors from two computers, with 4K60Hz and 4K120Hz listed. It provides 100W power delivery per connected PC, 1G Ethernet and an aluminum case, and it is plug and play.

It ranks second because it handles two computers, which the TobenONE does not, but supports fewer displays. It sits in the $100-200 bracket, so it is cheaper too.

Choose it if you share monitors between a laptop and a desktop. The caveat is that the 120Hz path applies to the setup the listing describes, so read it carefully.
products.idealFor: People sharing two monitors between two computers.
products.skipIf: You need more than two displays.

products.name: USB C Docking Station, Dual Monitor 4K@144Hz
products.verdict: Two monitors at up to 4K 144Hz for the lowest outlay.
products.description:
This USB-C dock supports two monitors at up to 4K 144Hz, with 2x HDMI and 2x DisplayPort outputs. It adds USB-A 2.0 and 3.0 ports, a 10Gbps USB-C 3.1 port, a 150W DC power input, Ethernet and card readers.

It ranks third because it supports only two displays and no KVM switching. It is the cheapest way here to reach a stated 144Hz. The listing falls in the $50-100 bracket.

Buy it for a dual 4K high-refresh desk on a budget. The caveat is that the listing's 144Hz figure needs a capable host to deliver it.
products.idealFor: Dual high-refresh desks on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want three or more displays.

products.name: AV Access 8K KVM Switch Dock, 2 Monitors 2 Computers
products.verdict: A KVM dock with an 8K ceiling and EDID emulation.
products.description:
The AV Access dock is a KVM switch for two monitors and two computers, with an 8K resolution ceiling and gigabit Ethernet. EDID emulation keeps display detection consistent when you switch, and it switches both displays and peripherals together.

It ranks fourth because the listing does not state a 4K 120Hz figure, unlike the KVM above it. Verify refresh before buying.

Choose it for a laptop-plus-desktop setup where consistent detection matters. The caveat is that refresh rate is not listed in our data.
products.idealFor: Switching two monitors between a laptop and a desktop.

products.name: Plugable Thunderbolt 4 Dock for M4/M5 MacBook (TBT-UDM)
products.verdict: Driverless native Thunderbolt video for M4 and M5 MacBooks.
products.description:
The Plugable TBT-UDM is a Thunderbolt 4 certified dock that needs no drivers. It supports dual 4K monitors or a single 6K display, with 100W charging for M4 and M5 MacBook Air and Pro. It has six USB ports, an SD card reader and Ethernet, and uses native Thunderbolt video rather than DisplayLink.

It ranks last because no 120Hz figure is stated, so it is a fit for Mac users who value driverless video over a published refresh rate. Expect it in the $100 to $200 bracket.

Choose it for an M4 or M5 MacBook. The caveat is verifying the refresh rate for your monitors.
products.idealFor: M4 and M5 MacBook owners who dislike drivers.

whatMatters.detail: Refresh rate is how often the picture updates, and 4K 120Hz needs bandwidth most docks lack. Many cap at 60Hz with two screens. Look for '4K@120Hz' in the title or bullets and check how many monitors it applies to.
DisplayLink compresses video over USB and needs a driver, while Thunderbolt carries video natively. The TobenONE is DisplayLink and the Plugable is native. The listing names which one it uses.
A KVM dock lets two computers share monitors and peripherals. It matters if you work on a laptop and a desktop. Look for 'KVM' and the number of computers supported.
Docks charge your laptop through the same cable. Wattage varies from 45W to 100W per PC. Match the number to your laptop's charger rating.
Some docks suit Windows, others Macs. The TobenONE 120Hz mode is for Windows with a driver. Check the compatibility line for your OS.

faq.a: No. Many cap at 60Hz, so check the listing for the stated figure. Three of the five here do.
They assume 4K support means 4K 120Hz. The refresh rate must be stated for the number of monitors you use.

faq.q: Is the TobenONE worth it over the budget dock?
faq.a: If you need more than two screens, yes. For two, the USB C 4K@144Hz dock costs far less.
The TobenONE DisplayLink dock requires one. The Plugable Thunderbolt dock is driverless.

faq.q: How do I keep a multi-monitor dock cool?
faq.a: The TobenONE has a built-in cooling fan. Give any dock airflow and avoid stacking items on it.

faq.q: Can a dock work with a Mac?
faq.a: The Plugable TBT-UDM is made for M4 and M5 MacBooks. The TobenONE 120Hz mode targets Windows.

finalTake: The TobenONE DL7400 is the best 4K 120Hz dock for Windows desks with several monitors. The KVM dock handles two computers, and the USB C 4K@144Hz dock is the budget route. Always confirm the refresh rate for your own monitor count.
